title: Unboxing Videos for Product Launches | AIVideosUGC
description: Plan unboxing videos for product launches: a teaser before, a full reveal on launch day, and a closer look after. See what to shoot and make your first clip.
h1: How to Use Unboxing Videos for Product Launches
lead: Unboxing videos for product launches work best as a short teaser, a reveal on launch day, and a closer look once people start asking what is in the box.
summary: Plan three short clips around launch day from one package photo, add the date and price yourself, and keep using the reveal after launch week.

paras: Why a launch uses three clips, which photo to start from, what the teaser, reveal, and closer look each do, how to write the scene, how long to make them, and where the date and price go.
sections.alt: Hands hold one plain cream ceramic travel mug above its open blank kraft parcel and tissue.

sections.h2: Why do unboxing videos for product launches work?
paras: A new product has not been seen in person yet. A short open answers what the box looks like, what is inside, and how big it is in someone's hands.

Three clips with different jobs are easier to plan than one long video. Tease the box before the day, show the full open on the day, and follow with a closer look once orders ship. The format fits earbuds, candles, skincare sets, and gift boxes, the kinds of products people open with a little anticipation.
sections.alt: Hands open a blank kraft parcel to reveal one plain cream ceramic travel mug wrapped in tissue.

sections.h2: What photo should a product launch unboxing video start from?
paras: Use a clear photo of the product in or next to the packaging people will actually receive, shot in daylight with any print facing the camera.

If the box design is still changing, wait until you can photograph the package people will receive. The clip follows that photo and the box you describe, so a stand-in becomes the box shoppers expect. Count what ships. If the kit includes a cable, a pouch, and a card, those are the items that should come out.
sections.alt: Hands place one plain cream ceramic travel mug beside its matching blank kraft parcel and folded tissue.

sections.h2: Which AI unboxing video ideas fit launch week?
paras: Plan a teaser, a reveal, and a closer look, each from the same package photo and each with its own sentence.

The teaser shows the closed box and a hand on the lid. The reveal opens the tissue and lifts the product out. The closer look turns one detail, such as a lid, a clasp, or a cable. [AI product video generator](page:product-videos) fits the closer look when you want a demo after the open. [AI image to video](page:image-to-video) fits when the still of the closed box should simply start to move.
sections.alt: Hands lift the lid of a blank kraft parcel to begin revealing one plain cream ceramic travel mug.

sections.h2: How do I write the scene for each launch clip?
paras: Name the box, the hands, and the one motion. Leave the date and the price out of that sentence.

The teaser can be "Hands rest on the lid of a plain kraft box, soft daylight." The reveal is "Hands lift the lid and raise one cream mug out of the tissue." The closer look names the one detail you want turned toward the camera. Keep each sentence to one motion.
sections.alt: Hands lift one plain cream ceramic mug with no lid from tissue inside a blank kraft parcel.

sections.h2: How long should an unboxing video for new products be?
paras: Use 6 seconds for the teaser, 10 to open and show the product, 15 for a slower reveal, and 30 for a multi-item kit.

Those lengths cost 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits. The cost shows before each job, and a failed job returns the credits. Use 9:16 for a short unboxing clip on TikTok, Reels, or Shorts, 1:1 for a feed, and 16:9 for a product page or a regular YouTube video. Each shape is a separate clip.
sections.alt: Hands set one plain cream ceramic travel mug beside its open blank kraft parcel after the reveal.

sections.h2: How do I add the date and price to a short unboxing clip?
paras: Download the clip and add the date, the price, and any code yourself in CapCut, Canva, TikTok, or Ads Manager.

Put the date and a few words such as "Coming soon" on the teaser. Put "Available now" and the price on the reveal. Add captions and music in the editor you already use, from a library cleared for ads. Post the teaser first, switch to the reveal when the product page is live, and save the closer look for the following week. Keep the teaser text short so it reads while the clip plays.
One real package photo, three sentences for teaser, reveal, and closer look, and your own date and price on top.
Do not show a box or a part the buyer will not receive. A 6, 10, 15, or 30 second clip is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits.

faq.q: What if the video shows something that is not in my box?
faq.a: Do not post that version. Make it again and name the exact contents, such as a bottle, a pump, and a pouch. Shoppers will compare their package with the open they saw.

faq.q: How long should an unboxing clip be?
faq.a: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Six is a teaser, ten opens and shows the product, fifteen is a slower reveal, and thirty covers a multi-item kit.

faq.q: What source photo should I use?
faq.a: Use a clear photo of the product or the package, and list every item in the box. Check the opening, the reveal, and the final contents against the real package.

faq.q: How many credits does an unboxing clip use?
faq.a: A 6-second clip uses 24 credits, 10 seconds uses 40, 15 uses 60, and 30 uses 120. A failed job returns the credits.

faq.q: What if my packaging is still changing?
faq.a: Wait until you can photograph the final package. Describe the box people will receive, not a stand-in.

faq.q: Can one package photo make several launch clips?
faq.a: Yes. Reuse the photo and write a separate sentence for the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look so each clip has one job.

cta_lead: Turn one package photo into a teaser, a reveal, or a follow-up clip, then check it against the real box.
